messages:
alex_chen: quick heads-up — prototyping an SLO-aware chargeback sketch that folds token-level cost + cache savings + model-sku amortization. want a quick sanity check.
maya: are we doing this per-tenant or per-route as a first pass?
jonathan: per-route first. then roll up to tenant. core idea: net_cost = marginal_token_cost - amortized_cache_savings, but adjusted for SLO tier (low-latency routes pay a premium). keep it simple initially.
sarah_p: main concern: how do we attribute shared cache hits? e.g. pooled KV caches where multiple routes benefit — naive attribution will over-credit some routes.
kevin_m: thought: tag cache entries with origin_route + ttl and attribute hits back proportionally by recent-origin frequencies. accurate but increases metadata and ETL. alternative: sampled attribution using request traces.
alex_chen: proto SQL snippet i used in the spike (very rough):
```
SELECT route,
       SUM(tokens)*price_per_token - SUM(cache_hit_tokens)*price_per_token*cache_credit AS net_cost
FROM tokens_raw
GROUP BY route;
```
(not final, just to show shape)
maya: for console UX: show two columns "Raw burn" and "SLO-adjusted net" and a toggle to switch. users kept getting confused by cache credits before.
jonathan: +1. also expose a "per-1k SLO-adjusted tokens" metric so PMs can compare routes independent of volume. tooltip should explain amortization window and routing assumptions.
billing-bot: FYI: adding route-level lineage to nightly ETL will bump job runtime ~12% and storage ~4GB/day.
sarah_p: :thumbsup: if we expose this in canary, we need a way to mark internal routes so they don't distort credits.
kevin_m: another edge: model fallback chains (A -> B) can double-count tokens if we don't attach a request_chain_id. propose request_id + step_index tagging on logs.
alex_chen: plan outline: 1) collect route tag + cache_hit_origin + request_chain_id at request time; 2) run nightly amortization that produces per-route credit rows; 3) console shows raw vs adjusted with drilldown to model-sku and cache lineage. who can pair on what?
maya: i can own the console bits (step 3). will pair with kevin on the data model.
jonathan: i'll formalize the amortization math (include burst windows and prefetch isolation so ephemeral prefetch doesn't get full credit).
sarah_p: please add a short FAQ blurb in the console explaining fairness assumptions and sampling limitations.
alex_chen: great — i'll open an RFC and a small spike ticket. tagging @kevin_m @maya @jonathan to review once i push the RFC. thanks everyone.
